speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin our evaluation of your acute diarrhea, how long have you been experiencing these symptoms, and have you noticed any blood or mucus in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: C. difficile infection (Clostridioides difficile colitis).

Given your recent treatment with levofloxacin for pneumonia and the onset of frequent watery diarrhea with abdominal cramping, this clinical picture is highly suggestive of an antibiotic-associated colitis. I will confirm this with a stool test for C. difficile toxins.
